description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06), the speed review the USER asked for.  docs/speed-review-s509.md; measurements and profiles in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/speed/ (prof.pl ROW... -> ROW.pl, ROW.lisp, ROW.prof; main b43188b5, gen v2-4280, load 5-6, best of 3-5)

PROFILE: `$s .= 'xy'` 10 M times (bench row catmod) spends 39 % SELF in the generic sequence function `replace` and 13.5 %
in `sb-kernel:ub32-bash-copy`; catself 36 % + 16 %; listdeclcat 23 % + 9 %; joinarr (`join(',', @a)`) 27 % + 9 %.
CAUSE (read): cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%pcl-str-blit` has an inline arm for n = 1 (a previous round) and calls
`(replace data s ...)` for everything else with S declared only `string`, so SBCL cannot open-code the copy.

HAND-REPLACED A/B (TAKEN; `leverA.lisp` in that directory redefines `%pcl-str-blit` / `%pcl-str-append` and is loaded in
front of the unchanged transpiled programs): one more arm -- when S is `(simple-array character (*))`, an inline loop for
n <= 16 and a both-sides-typed `replace` above that:
     row          perl    main    typed copy
     catmod       0.206   0.603   0.290   (-52 %)
     catself      0.248   0.582   0.270   (-54 %)
     listdeclcat  0.169   0.352   0.238   (-32 %)
     strcat       0.439   0.424   0.439   (noise: the 1-char shape was already inline)

SCOPE (rule 11 -- ONE helper, used at each site): (1) `%pcl-str-blit`; (2) `%p-join-strings` (joinarr: 36 % in replace +
bash-copy); (3) the concatenation behind `p-string-concat` / `p-.` for 2-3 pieces (lcbytes: `%concatenate-to-string` is 29 %
total); (4) the `:strbuf` cell's append that s507p's round 39 adds (#2115 (c)) -- so this round starts AFTER s507p is merged.
A simple-base-string source needs its own arm or a widening copy; a non-simple source keeps the generic call.

BARS: the hand-replaced A/B per site BEFORE the edit (expected -20 to -30 % on joinarr / lcbytes; not measured), the
whole-table bench with control rows, gate + sweep (a runtime-only change: corpus-diff IDENTICAL), `PCL_STRBUF_AUDIT` logs
empty.  Rule-12 read of each touched dispatch: the new arm must not make a string type fall through.
subject: PERF, MEASURED s509 (lever A): the string buffer's append calls GENERIC `replace` to copy 2 characters -- a typed short copy in `%pcl-str-blit` takes catmod 0.603 -> 0.290 s (-52 %), catself 0.582 -> 0.270 (-54 %), listdeclcat 0.352 -> 0.238 (-32 %); the same call shape is in join, 3-way concat and the :strbuf append
